about:
# Arachnophobia Shield — WoW Forever Addon

Addon for **World of Warcraft Forever** (classic 1.x-line client, v1.60.1)
that covers spider models with a nameplate-attached UI element. UI-layer
only: no model swaps, no game-file modification. Covers are always
click-through and always fully opaque.

**Status: v1.2.0.** This README documents current behavior only; the
change history lives in Git.

## How it works

- Every cover is a child of the spider's **nameplate**, so native plate
  movement and scale carry the cover between polling ticks. No targeting,
  mouseover or input is needed; tracking is on by default.
- Cover size is a **percentage of the nameplate width** (`/as scale`,
  whole number `40`–`130`, `100` = default).
- **Near-field boost (automatic):** the client holds nameplate apparent
  size in a narrow band (~73–90 UI px) while the model keeps growing as
  you close in, so a plate-proportional cover would under-cover close
  spiders. Every 10 Hz tick multiplies the tracked size by a smooth ramp
  of the plate's apparent width: no boost at/under 75 UI px, full ×3.0 at/
  above 85 UI px. There is no setting to change it; `/as debug on` shows
  the per-plate values on the `AS| near:` line.
- When the client removes a dead unit's nameplate, the cover goes with
  it. When the addon observes an accessible spider death, a centered,
  click-through **LOOK AWAY** warning appears for 1.75 seconds. It warns
  that the corpse may be visible; it does not cover the body.

## Install

The addon ships as a single ZIP. Either let an AI coding agent do it
end-to-end or follow the manual steps; both end with the same ZIP
extracted into your game's `Interface/AddOns/` directory. Prebuilt
release ZIPs are attached to
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/evelyn-loves-coffee/ArachnophobiaShield/releases);
they are generated by the build below and are never checked into the
repository.

### Option A — let an AI agent do it

If you run a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, pi, …), point it at the
game folder and ask, for example:

> Clone
> https://github.com/evelyn-loves-coffee/ArachnophobiaShield.git, build
> the release ZIP with `uv run --with lupa python
> tools/package_addon.py`, then extract the ZIP into my WoW Forever
> `Interface/AddOns` directory so that
> `AddOns/ArachnophobiaShield/ArachnophobiaShield.toc` exists. Verify
> the final folder layout before finishing.

The agent clones the repo, runs the build (which also re-runs the
addon's offline Lua test suite against the packaged files) and places
the folder. If your agent runs on a different machine than the game,
have it produce the ZIP and copy that one file over.

### Option B — manual

**Prerequisites:** `git` and
[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Nothing else — `uv run --with lupa`
below installs Python if you don't have one and fetches `lupa` (a Lua
5.1 binding) automatically.

Clone and build from the repository root:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/evelyn-loves-coffee/ArachnophobiaShield.git
cd ArachnophobiaShield
uv run --with lupa python tools/package_addon.py
```

The build writes `dist/ArachnophobiaShield-<version>-fixed.zip`
(currently `dist/ArachnophobiaShield-1.2.0-fixed.zip`), validates the
package contents and prints its SHA-256 and size.

**Deploy:** unzip the ZIP directly into your game's
`Interface/AddOns/` directory so the `.toc` sits at
`Interface/AddOns/ArachnophobiaShield/ArachnophobiaShield.toc`, without
an extra nested `ArachnophobiaShield/ArachnophobiaShield/` folder. When
updating over an existing install, extract on top of the folder; your
`Custom/` images and saved settings live inside it (re-copy any custom
images if you replaced the whole folder).

Typical `Interface/AddOns/` locations. The client subfolder is
`_classic_beta_` in the current development build and **may change when
the Forever client ships**, so treat the names below as examples: the
`AddOns` folder is always the `AddOns` subfolder of the folder that
contains the game's `Interface/` directory (e.g.
`<game root>\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\` on a stock install):

| OS | Example path |
| :-- | :-- |
| Windows | `C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\` (also seen: `C:\Program Files\…` or `C:\World of Warcraft\…`) |
| Linux (Steam/Proton) | `~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/<app-id>/pfx/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/` |
| Linux (Wine) | `~/.wine/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/` (path varies with your Wine prefix) |

Log in or `/reload`; `/as version` reports the
version and `/as selftest` reports the live tracking state.

Enable **enemy nameplates** in the game options. The addon starts enabled
on a fresh install; `/as enable` also enables tracking and retries paused
coverage. `/as disable` stops tracking and hides every cover (stays
disabled after reload).

## Slash commands

| Command | Effect |
| :-- | :-- |
| `/as` | usage (identical to `/as help`) |
| `/as version` | print the addon version and the client's build / interface / Lua versions |
| `/as selftest` | diagnostics: enabled, tracked, covers shown, limited / paused |
| `/as config` | open the cover picker with preview, presets and custom-image path |
| `/as cover <choice>` | select `fox`, `red`, `blue`, `sage`, `charcoal`, or `custom <local .tga path>` |
| `/as enable` | enable tracking and retry paused coverage; enabled by default |
| `/as disable` | stop tracking and hide every cover; stays disabled after reload |
| `/as toggle` | switch between enabled tracking and disabled covers |
| `/as scale [N]` | cover size as a **percentage** of the nameplate width, whole number `40`–`130`, `100` = default |
| `/as drop [N]` | how far below the nameplate it sits (`0`–`4`, default `0.3`) |
| `/as name <name>` | add an **exact** creature name to a local list (spaces allowed); as of v1.2.0 the list no longer affects coverage (detection is family-only) |
| `/as names` | list the names in the local list |
| `/as forget <name>` | remove a name from the local list |
| `/as reset` | restore every saved setting to its factory default and reapply |
| `/as debug [on\|off]` | verbose decisions for bug reports (off by default) |
| `/as help` | usage |

`/as on` and `/as off` remain compatibility aliases for enable/disable.

## How a spider is recognised

A creature is covered only when the client files it as creature family
**`Spider`** (id 3) — the addon's sole detection signal as of v1.2.0.
That covers every creature the game itself files as a spider, and
nothing else.

v1.2.0 retired the earlier fallbacks — name fragments (`spider`,
`tarantula`, `webspinner`, `widow`, `skitterer`, `webwood`, …) and the
`/as name` extra-name list: fragment matching kept covering non-spiders
(a "Lake Creeper" matched the `creeper` fragment), so coverage is now
strictly family-based. The `/as name` / `/as names` / `/as forget`
commands still manage the local name list, but the list no longer
affects coverage.

Detection is **best-effort**: a spider-like creature filed outside the
Spider family (for example, a "Crypt Horror") goes unidentified. Player
units are excluded.

**Everything stays local.** The name list and all settings are stored
only in the addon's SavedVariables on your machine; they are never
uploaded, transmitted or reported anywhere.

## Custom cover images

The picker has no file browser by design: the addon never enumerates the
game's filesystem. Put a `.tga` in the addon's `Custom\` folder and point
the addon at it with the picker or `/as cover custom
Interface\AddOns\ArachnophobiaShield\Custom\.tga` (path relative to
the game root, backslashes; a bare file name is rejected — the picker
prefills the required prefix). A navy backing is drawn behind custom
images, so transparency in your art shows navy, not the world.

Full setup, the PNG/JPEG conversion helper and the symptom-by-symptom
troubleshooting table: [docs/COVER-IMAGES.md](https://github.com/evelyn-loves-coffee/ArachnophobiaShield/blob/main/docs/COVER-IMAGES.md).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
| :-- | :-- |
| No covers at all | Enemy nameplates disabled in game options? Check `/as selftest` for `limited=true`; run `/as enable` (also retries after `paused=true`). |
| `/as selftest` reports `limited=true` | One or more client reads were unavailable; covers may be incomplete. Re-run `/as selftest` after `/reload`; report if it persists. |
| Close spider shows legs | `/as scale 120` and/or `/as drop 0.5`; the automatic near boost already caps at ×3.0. |
| Cover off the model | Nameplate stacking/clamping moved the plate itself — a client behavior no UI-layer addon can correct (see below). |
| Custom image not loading | See the table in [docs/COVER-IMAGES.md](https://github.com/evelyn-loves-coffee/ArachnophobiaShield/blob/main/docs/COVER-IMAGES.md). |

## Known limitations

- This client exposes **no world-to-screen projection** or enemy position
  API, so the cover can only follow the nameplate. Stacking or screen-edge
  clamping by the game can move the plate away from the model.
- The client **fades nameplates with distance** (and covers are nameplate
  children), so covers fade too; this cannot be disabled from an addon.
  The camouflage presets exist to make a spider's outline hard to trace
  through that fade. There is no opacity control.
- Very close models can extend beyond a cover even at the ×3.0 ceiling.
- Deaths not observed through accessible unit data can be missed by the
  look-away warning.

## AI disclosure

The majority of the code in this addon was written by open-weight AI
models running entirely on local hardware; a very small amount of
coding was assisted by cloud-based AI API services. The maintainer
directed and reviewed the work throughout development.

## Credits and data

Arachnophobia Shield is an independent **spiritual successor to the
accessibility approach** of [NoSpider - Arachnophobia Mode](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/nospider-arachnophobia-mode)
by **GrasHopper42**. No NoSpider code, artwork, bundled libraries,
zone tables, spawn coordinates or creature lists have been copied or
bundled; its native parent-and-anchor overlay approach informed this
implementation.

No creature database is bundled: detection relies solely on the
client's creature-family signal. No zone tables or spawn datasets are
bundled or required for the nameplate overlay.

## Developer documentation

Maintainer handoff — design constraints, client API facts, tracking
model, test procedure and data-source rules: [docs/HANDOFF.md](https://github.com/evelyn-loves-coffee/ArachnophobiaShield/blob/main/docs/HANDOFF.md).

## License

The supplied fox artwork is included with the user's permission to publish
it with this addon; the code license does not grant a separate license to
reuse that artwork elsewhere.

releases.notes:
UI-layer spider covers for arachnophobia — WoW Forever (classic 1.x-line client, v1.60.1).

Install: extract the attached ZIP into the game's `Interface/AddOns/` directory so the .toc sits at `AddOns/ArachnophobiaShield/ArachnophobiaShield.toc`. Full instructions (including the AI-agent and manual build paths) are in the README packaged inside the ZIP.

`/as version` in game reports the loaded version; `/as selftest` reports live tracking state.
